lines.text: Testing. Right. Day two at Kestrel-4. Dispatch wants a spoken log as well as the written one, so this is the spoken log.
The generator's a beast and the breaker's worse. The view from the north window is nothing at all, which I'm told is the point.
Hollis's mug is still on its hook. I've left it there. Felt rude to move it.
(click)
Day eight. I'm recording this because I want a voice in the room that isn't the generator.
I asked Imogen for Hollis's file. She says there isn't one. Eighteen months on station and no file.
Tracks again this morning, up to the west door. I'm not going out to look at them. I'm saying that on tape so it counts.
(click)
(wind, very close to the microphone) Day fourteen. Outside, on the tether. I'm recording because if I'm talking, I'm not listening.
Post four. Post five. There's... no. Keep walking.
(footsteps in the snow, two sets, not quite in time)
At the mast. North gauge twelve under. Heading back now. Not turning round. Not turning round.
(click)
Kestrel-4, keeper Hollis. Day... a hundred and something. Just gone three.
For the record, since the Service likes a record: it knocked three times again. I've decided it's polite. It always waits to be asked.
Imogen says the pressure data is the best they've ever had. She says I'm doing important work. She says it the way you'd talk to a horse.
If you've found this, I expect I've gone to have a look. Don't come after me. It's warm out there, it says. I expect that's true.
(click)
Last tape. The real Imogen called at nine. Relief flight at six, she said. She sounded tired. She sounded like a person.
The other one called at ten to three. It sounded better than her.
Whoever you are: the door. Only the door. Whatever it says, wherever the light is. Six o'clock. You can do it. I nearly could.
(click)
